A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same C3B benchmark. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of eleven MLLMs, a Q1/Q2 prompting ablation, culture-specific analyses, and a human comparison in Sections 5.1–5.6.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and additionally reports an OCR experiment, annotation-quality statistics, and human agreement and response-time results.

M1.justification: The three benchmark tasks, comic-generation pipeline, conflict annotation, and Translator–Reviewer process are retained. Added screening and annotation instructions document construction more fully without establishing a changed underlying method.

E1.justification: Appendix H adds an OCR-derived source-text condition for the existing Manga109 translation task in JA-DE, JA-RU, JA-ES, and JA-TH. This modestly extends input-condition coverage; the datasets, main tasks, languages, and cultural coverage otherwise remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 3–4 retain the same eleven MLLMs, and the human comparator remains. The new OCR ablation uses three existing models—Qwen2.5-VL, LLaVA1.5-7B, and Llama3.2—and introduces no new model baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix H introduces a controlled comparison of pre-extracted Manga109 text and PaddleOCR-extracted text, evaluated using BLEU for three models across four translation directions. Table 7 additionally reports response time. Existing main evaluation metrics, CACC weights, and sampling of 100 human-study questions per difficulty tier are retained.

E4.justification: The new OCR ablation tests sensitivity to text extraction, while Appendix E adds annotation-quality analysis through correction and agreement statistics. The Q1/Q2 ablation, cultural breakdown, and model error cases are retained; the case-study appendix moves from E to F.

E5.justification: V2 first reports annotation agreement of 76.8% in Appendix E and human inter-rater agreement of 95%, 91%, and 93% across difficulty tiers in Table 7. It adds no repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 3–6 and Table 7's accuracy results are unchanged. Table 8 adds OCR-condition BLEU scores: for example, Qwen2.5-VL scores 1.32 versus 14.5 without OCR on JA-ES, while Llama3.2 scores 2.73 versus 0.99 on JA-TH. New results also include human response times and annotation corrections affecting 237 images and questions associated with 755 images.

T1.justification: The CACC, correlation, CDPI, CBI, and CAD formulas are unchanged. The three diversity measures become displayed Equations 3–5 with expanded explanations; no new mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: a comic-based, multicultural and multilingual benchmark with three progressively difficult tasks, evaluations of eleven MLLMs, and a substantial human–model performance gap.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 and the new ethics statement explicitly interpret cultural conflict as distinct cultures co-occurring, rather than aggression. Appendix H also adds the interpretation that the main translation weaknesses cannot be attributed to OCR because the main experiments used pre-extracted text.

D1.justification: New Appendix E substantially expands the previously generic manual-verification description with annotator backgrounds and roles, work allocation, independent and collective review, source checking, and cultural granularity and exclusion guidelines. V2 also documents prompt screening and identifies PaddleOCR for the additional experiment. These are substantial reproducibility disclosures, not evidence that the benchmark was rebuilt.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds discussion and citations for GLOBALRG, ALM-bench, AlKhamissi et al. (2025), and Karamolegkou et al. (2024). This broadens the cultural-benchmark context while retaining the existing contribution positioning.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, expands metric explanations, adds author notes and acknowledgements, and introduces ethics, annotation, and OCR sections. The main narrative and existing appendix content remain largely intact, with corresponding appendix renumbering.

P2.justification: Table 7 gains agreement and timing columns, and Table 8 is added. Figures 1–2 receive acronym corrections, Figure 3 relabels verification stages, and Figure 5 receives a clearer caption. Displayed equations, conference headers, and content reflow produce limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: Annotation guidelines, agreement statistics, and the OCR control improve transparency and interpretation of the retained results. The gains are limited by new reporting inconsistencies: Section 5.6 describes graduate human evaluators while Appendix G retains undergraduates, and the blanket OCR-degradation interpretation overlooks Llama3.2's JA-TH increase from 0.99 to 2.73 in Table 8.
